newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Philippine stocks surge on GNP data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Philippine stocks surge on GNP data.

text.p: Philippine shares shot up on Friday after the government announced strong economic growth figures and even though economists said the growth was not high enough, analysts said.

"People were probably pleased with the GNP (gross national product) results. In the first place, the market is starved for good news and the GNP result while not too bullish was still favourable," said Francisco Trinidad, research head at DBS Securities Phils.
The main index pierced a 2,800 point resistance to close at the day's high of 2,809.45 points, up 51 points and its seventh consecutive rise.

After the market had closed on Thursday, the government said GNP had risen 6.1 percent in the first quarter, down on below its own projection of a 6.4 percent rise and lower than the 6.9 percent a year earlier.
Economists warned that the government will have a tough time meeting its seven to eight percent growth target for the year.
"Although GNP did not live up to the 1996 level, the consensus view was really for a slower growth rate," Patricia Hocson, analyst at Anscor Hagedorn Securities, said.
"Hence, a figure lower than the government's expectations may not necessarily be construed as inhibiting the market. Our bet is that this has already been discounted by most players," she added.
Other analysts said that first quarter GNP may have dispelled fears that the Philippines is set for a property crash, a battered currency and a general economic slowdown similar to Thailand.
Such concerns earlier this month prompted investors, mostly foreigners, to flee the market, hitting property and banking issues.

"The Thailand comparison was a big factor in the recent slump of the market. The economic comparison growth figures showed that we are not like Thailand and this improved the market's fragile sentiment," said Allan Araullo, vice-president at Regina Capital Development Corp.
Week-on-week, the market barometer gained 211 points, rising almost eight percent from the previous week's 2,598.20.
Traders, however, have yet to be convinced of a reversal as market has been trading on moribund volumes.
"Next week, we just have to see the market consolidate. Too steep and too fast a runup in the last seven days is just not healthy," said Jidgette Valenzuela, research manager at Lippo Securities.
